title: Key and mouse glyphs in the toolbar instead of text
user-messages:
> Still open from before: crease hover speed (awaiting your pick between the two options), and why your two-anchor crease ring crossed itself.

could we get some glyphs instead of test only
description: The toolbar along the bottom of every model scene lists the active tool's controls as text: 'enter: confirm draft', 'shift+T: ...', 'drag: ...'. Show a glyph for each key and mouse action instead of the word. The font atlas (opensans.json / opensans.png, built by msdf-atlas-gen) holds only the 95 ASCII characters 32-126, and msdf-atlas-gen is not installed on the dev machine, so the icons have to be added to the atlas (SpecialGlyphs already maps private-use characters to atlas cells, with one entry, COLOR_TRACKER) or drawn from a second SDF texture. Glyphs wanted first: enter, shift, ctrl, esc, backspace/delete, mouse click, mouse drag; letter keys as a keycap around the letter. The toolbar is drawn in Scene.drawUI from the TOOL_SECTION control hints (ControlHint.key is the label to replace).
definition-of-done:
1. Enter, shift, ctrl, esc, delete/backspace, click and drag show as glyphs in the toolbar, letter keys as keycaps.
2. A key with no glyph still shows its text label.
3. The glyphs read at the toolbar's row height in both palettes; screenshot under tmp/.
4. FontAtlasPaddingTest still passes if the atlas is rebuilt.

Keeps the existing ConnectionTool rings-as-walls, RingRegionTool drop-part-names, RingTool fit-every-ring and StrokeSculptTool save log lines: they are on master already, moved unchanged out of control-row lambdas into methods.
testing-plan:
1. Launch the ring scene, open the ring tool and its drawing mode, screenshot the toolbar: every listed key shows its glyph.
2. Unit test: a control hint whose key has no glyph is drawn as its text label.
3. Run FontAtlasPaddingTest.
unknowns: Rebuild the OpenSans atlas with an icon font merged in, or load a second small SDF atlas for icons?
Which icon set: it must be permissively licensed (MIT, BSD, Apache, OFL).
changes-made: Second MSDF atlas res/keyglyphs.png/.json built by tools/build_key_glyphs.py (keycaps with OpenSans labels, authored mouse glyphs, Apache-2.0 MDI symbols for enter/shift/backspace/arrows/move) with the settings opensans.json uses; Font draws private-use chars from it in a second pass; KeyGlyphs.label maps hint keys; InfoPane and SceneModelMenu controls show them. Toolbar (UI-21) still to switch to KeyGlyphs.label.

Synced onto master after UI-21 landed; ToolbarPane draws KeyGlyphs.label (no colon after a glyph key). Word keycaps and mouse strokes enlarged. KeyGlyphsTest: text fallback, glyph mapping, atlas holds every glyph. Screenshots tmp/ui-20-toolbar-{dark,paper}.png.

Glyphs now come from the binding, not the label: KeyGlyphs maps a key code (forKeyCode) or a MouseGesture (forGesture) to a glyph and knows nothing of ControlHint; ControlHint.glyphLabel() puts ctrl/shift keycaps before it from controlHeld/shiftHeld and falls back to the text label. Mouse rows use ControlHint.mouse(MouseGesture, ...) (new enum in platform.input). 'drag anchor'/'drag pick' descriptions now name what is dragged. ToolbarPaneTest expects the glyph label.

Keys is now an enum holding each key's code, glyph and label; CLICK, DRAG, SCROLL and DOUBLE_CLICK are Keys too, so KeyGlyphs and MouseGesture are gone. ControlHint holds a Keys and no label string: keyLabel() builds the text, glyphLabel() the glyphs. Every control row passes only its Keys; int key codes compare against Keys.X.keyCode.

Ring tool: T calls switchMode(), shift+T fitEveryCreaseRingToGeodesic(), and both fit through the one fitDraftToGeodesic(); row actions across RingScene, ConnectionTool, ClosedRingTool, RingRegionTool, StrokeSculptTool, Scene, ModelScene and TradeScene are methods, not lambda bodies (TradeScene Esc overrides escapePressed, so terminal ex matches it).

Font: one drawLayers(atlas, ...) draws whichever atlas's pass is set up (a glyph draws only in the atlas holding it, the other's only advance the pen); drawWords runs it for the text, then for key glyphs in their own pass. drawTextNoSetup and the keyGlyphPass flag removed. Full build 806 tests green; screenshots retaken.
review-summary: Control hints in the toolbar and controls lists draw keys and mouse actions as glyphs (keycaps, mice) from a second MSDF atlas that Font draws alongside the text atlas. Glyphs read faster than words like "shift+drag", and keys without a glyph keep their text.
